title: Sitecore to Strapi: headless content architecture
subtitle: Life insurance client · Publicis Sapient
summary: Content architecture for a Sitecore-to-Strapi migration, defining the information architecture, structured content model and reusable templates and components.

artwork.alt: Neon pink connected content blocks representing structured content architecture.

facts.label: Client
facts.value: Life insurance client, via Publicis Sapient

facts.label: Output
facts.value: Sitemap, information architecture, content model, taxonomy and tagging strategy, template and component structure

story.label: Context
story.title: Moving to a headless CMS
story.body: A life insurance client was migrating from Sitecore to Strapi and needed a content architecture that could support a scalable website.

story.label: My role
story.title: Shaping the structure behind the site
story.body: As Content Architect, I worked with the marketing lead to define the sitemap, information architecture, content model, taxonomy and tagging strategy. I partnered with UX and developers to translate these into reusable templates and components.

story.label: Outcome
story.title: A scalable foundation in Strapi
story.body: The result was a website powered by a headless CMS, with structured content and reusable components designed to support future growth.

title: Connecting FAQs with chatbot answers
subtitle: NatWest Group · Accenture
summary: Restructured FAQ content across five NatWest Group brands, connecting personal and business banking answers with websites and a chatbot.

artwork.alt: Neon pink line diagram of FAQ content connecting to a chatbot.

story.label: Challenge
story.title: One content source. More ways to find an answer.
story.body: Across five NatWest Group brands, personal and business banking FAQs were held in a legacy CMS. To connect this content with a chatbot, the answers needed to be audited, cleaned and restructured before migration to Adobe Experience Manager (AEM).

story.label: Content architecture
story.title: Making the answers work harder
story.body: I audited the existing FAQ content and refined its structure and consistency. The focus was on preparing questions and answers for use across the website and chatbot, with a tagging approach to support content organisation and retrieval.

story.label: Implementation
story.title: From legacy content to AEM
story.body: I worked with a technical architect to write the migration script, connecting the content restructuring work with the technical move into AEM. The chatbot integration formed part of the same programme.

story.label: Outcome
story.title: Launched across web and chatbot
story.body: The project launched with restructured FAQ content in AEM and an integrated chatbot. It also improved the authoring experience for the teams maintaining personal and business banking answers across the five brands.

title: From WordPress to structured content
subtitle: Schroders Personal Wealth · Publicis Sapient
summary: Designed the content architecture for a WordPress-to-Contentful migration, translating UX, components and templates into a structured content model.

artwork.alt: Neon pink line diagram of website content being organised into reusable components.

story.label: Challenge
story.title: A new CMS needed a new content foundation
story.body: Schroders Personal Wealth was moving its website from WordPress to Contentful. The UX, components and templates needed a coherent structure behind them, with clear content models and a practical approach to moving existing material into the new platform.

story.label: Content architecture
story.title: Modelling the whole website
story.body: I content-modelled the entire site, translating the experience and template requirements into structured content. Alongside this, I audited existing material, mapped content to the new structure and shaped the content design and taxonomy.

story.label: Author enablement
story.title: Preparing the people who would publish
story.body: The implementation included author training so the team could manage and publish content in Contentful. This connected the new architecture with the day-to-day work of maintaining the website after launch.

story.label: Outcome
story.title: A launched website with structure behind it
story.body: The website launched on Contentful with a site-wide content model, mapped content and trained authors. The programme brought content architecture, migration preparation and publishing practice together as part of the platform change.
